description: Contrato de render por tipo: forma de content + correct_answer que el Lesson Engine realmente dibuja/califica. Fuente para el prompt del generador y el gate de render-compat.

price_detective.content_shape: content.items: [{id, name|label|text, price, quantity?, unit?, icon?}, ...]. Supports pairwise shapes (products/items/options/prices/stores/cases/markets/cities per resolveOptions line 35).
price_detective.answer_shape: correct_answer.itemId (canonical) — also accepts: correctProductId, correctId, selectedId, correctOptionId
render_gotchas: resolveOptions must find the items array under one of 7 keys (line 35) — if items live under an unlisted key, component renders empty
hasPriceData check (line 46) returns false if no product.price > 0 — disables 'Investigate' button and never shows unit prices, component becomes choice-only
name/label/text fallback (line 39) — if item lacks all three, renders blank product name
Grader (useLessonState line 459) accepts multi-answer only via correctOptionIds array, not trapIds (which are only for spot_trap)
price_detective.canonical_example: {"content": {"scenario": "Mira el diario de Pablo.", "instruction": "¿En qué día gastó más dinero?", "items": [{"id": "d1", "label": "Martes", "price": 6}, {"id": "d2", "label": "Jueves", "price": 4}, {"id": "d3", "label": "Sábado", "price": 8}]}, "correct_answer": {"itemId": "d3"}}

quiz_battle.content_shape: content.question: string + content.options: [{id, text|label}, ...] (single-question real JSON format, line 42-48) OR content.questions: [{question, options:[{id, text}], correctId?}, ...] (legacy multi-question, line 39-41). Grader reads options array to locate options; correctId lives in question object or at exercise.correct_answer level.
quiz_battle.answer_shape: correct_answer.correctOptionId (canonical) — also accepts: correctId, choiceId. Grader line 114 checks question.correctId first (legacy), then exercise.correct_answer.correctOptionId, then exercise.correct_answer.correctId. Component score passed to grader; grader checks score >= minScore (line 998) derived from questionCount * 100.
render_gotchas: questions array must exist; if neither content.questions nor (content.question + content.options) present, renders 'Sin preguntas disponibles' fallback (line 100)
Grader (useLessonState line 989-999): minScore defaults to questionCount * 100 — for single-question quiz must score >= 100, not the old hardcoded 200
Component emits score (sum of points), NOT boolean — grader expects numeric comparison vs threshold (line 990)
options missing from question object → map(option) renders empty array (line 198), component displays no choices
quiz_battle.canonical_example: {"content": {"question": "¿Cuál es la diferencia CRUCIAL en el perfil de riesgo entre comprar una propiedad directa e invertir en una FIBRA?", "instruction": "Selecciona la afirmación más precisa.", "options": [{"id": "a", "text": "La propiedad directa tiene riesgo de iliquidez y costos altos; la FIBRA tiene riesgo de volatilidad del precio en bolsa."}, {"id": "b", "text": "Ambas tienen exactamente el mismo riesgo porque ambas son bienes raíces."}, {"id": "c", "text": "La FIBRA es más riesgosa porque no puedes vivir en el edificio."}]}, "correct_answer": {"correctOptionId": "a"}}

spot_trap.content_shape: content.traps: [{id, text, isTrap}, ...] (primary shape, line 35-40) or content.messages/scenarios/statements/items/plans/segments/etc with isTrap flag. Fallback to content.options/choices if no message/scenario array found. Grader reads from: correctAnswer.trapIds (array), or correctAnswer + any of: correctTraps/targetIds/correctOptionIds/redFlagIds/trapSegmentIds/trapLineIds/trapsFound (line 761-763), or content items with isTrap flag (line 776-781), or extractCorrectId (line 768-771).
spot_trap.answer_shape: correct_answer.trapIds: string[] (canonical) — also accepts: correctTraps, targetIds, correctOptionIds, redFlagIds, trapSegmentIds, trapLineIds, trapsFound, or single id via extractCorrectId (targetId, trapId, trapStatementId, etc.). Grader line 753-788 checks selectedTraps (user Set) === correctTraps (Set), exact match of size and membership.
render_gotchas: Container keys tried in order (line 35-40): messages, scenarios, traps, statements, items, plans, planSteps, etc. — if data stored under a key not in this list, fallback mode triggers (line 110 isFallbackMode)
isTrap flag must exist on trap items; items with neither isTrap nor isCorrect treated as safe (line 47: isTrap = it?.isTrap ?? it?.isCorrect ?? false)
Fallback mode (line 110) switches to rendering content.options/choices as button list instead of message cards — no trap count validation, just single-select (line 100-106)
Grader (line 753-788): trapIds array is required; single-id extractCorrectId returns selectedTraps.size === 1 (line 771), not array comparison. Mismatch causes silent 'return false'
spot_trap.canonical_example: {"content": {"scenario": "Un amigo te dice: 'Las FIBRAS son la mejor inversión. Su gráfico histórico solo sube y los dividendos son altísimos. Es dinero seguro.'", "instruction": "Identifica dos 'trampas' o afirmaciones engañosas en su argumento.", "traps": [{"id": "t1", "text": "Afirmar que el gráfico 'solo sube' ignora las correcciones y caídas periódicas.", "isTrap": true}, {"id": "t2", "text": "Decir que los dividendos son 'altísimos' sin contexto puede esconder riesgo.", "isTrap": false}, {"id": "t3", "text": "Llamar 'dinero seguro' a cualquier inversión en bolsa es incorrecto.", "isTrap": true}]}, "correct_answer": {"trapIds": ["t1", "t3"]}}

classification.content_shape: content.categories: [{id, name|label|text|title}, ...] (line 66, reads catLabel via line 69 fallback chain name||label||text||title). content.items: [{id, text, correctCategoryId|correctCategory}, ...] (line 29-36). Grader normalizeClassifications (line 262-328) accepts: direct Record<itemId, categoryId>, inverted {categoryKey: [itemIds]}, array-of-objects [{itemId, categoryId}], or extracted from content.items.correctCategory.
classification.answer_shape: correct_answer: Record<itemId, categoryId> or inverted {categoryKey: [itemIds]} or [{itemId, categoryId}, ...] (grader normalizes all to canonical Record form). Component emits Record<itemId, categoryId> (line 19, 42-45). Grader (line 630-644) normalizes both correct_answer and compares: every item must match.
render_gotchas: catLabel fallback (line 69) critical — reads name||label||text||title in order; if all missing, renders empty category header
content.items missing or empty → no items render; grader line 641 iterates over content.items, so mismatch in data shape causes 'return false'

normalizeClassifications wrapper keys (line 272-275): classifications, categoryAssignments, mappings, matches, categoryItems, etc. — if data structure uses different wrapper name, normalization fails, grader 'return true' (line 636 fallback)

Inverted format {categoryId: [itemId]} resolved via buildCategoryResolver (line 229-243) which matches category name||label||title to id — if category names in data mismatch corpus, resolver returns string(k) unmapped, category comparison fails silently
classification.canonical_example: {"content": {"statement": "Clasifica estos gastos de la semana", "instruction": "Arrastra cada gasto a su día correcto", "categories": [{"id": "cat1", "label": "Lunes 🟡"}, {"id": "cat2", "label": "Miércoles 🟢"}, {"id": "cat3", "label": "Viernes 🔵"}], "items": [{"id": "i1", "text": "🍦 Helado", "correctCategoryId": "cat2"}, {"id": "i2", "text": "📚 Cuaderno", "correctCategoryId": "cat1"}, {"id": "i3", "text": "🎾 Pelota", "correctCategoryId": "cat3"}]}, "correct_answer": {"cat1": ["i2"], "cat2": ["i1"], "cat3": ["i3"]}}

risk_reward.content_shape: content.decision (or content.question, content.scenario) — string; content.risk_options (or content.options) — array of {id: string, type: 'risk'|'safe', text?: string, title?: string, label?: string, reward?: string} — renderer reads option.type to pick icon (AlertTriangle vs ShieldCheck) and option.reward to show on reveal
risk_reward.answer_shape: correct_answer.correctOptionId (string) — the canonical risk/safe choice id. Aliases: correctChoiceId, correctId, choiceId, preferredOption, betterOption, selectedId, selectedOptionId. Grader uses optionIdMatches() for tolerance to prefixes (mindset, approach, option, plan, offer, strategy, choice, item, product, etc.)
render_gotchas: risk_options[] not resolved — renderer calls resolveOptions(content, ['risk_options', 'options']) so must provide one of these keys, not bare items

option.type missing or wrong value — only 'risk' triggers coral icon + AlertTriangle; anything else gets emerald + ShieldCheck. If you mix 'Risk'/'RISK' (capitalized), type coercion fails → all render as safe
option.reward undefined — Revealed box on select shows 'undefined'. Must provide reward string for every option
correct_answer with plural form (correctOptionIds array) — grader treats as multi-select, rejects single choice. Use singular correctOptionId for single-select risk_reward
Decision text (decision/question/scenario) — renderer picks in order (content.decision > content.question > content.scenario > i18n fallback). If none exist, breaks layout. Must provide at least one
risk_reward.canonical_example: {"content": {"decision": "Te ofrecen consolidar deudas en un préstamo más largo. ¿Cuál es el mayor riesgo?", "risk_options": [{"id": "a", "type": "risk", "title": "Pagar más intereses", "reward": "Identificaste el verdadero riesgo."}, {"id": "b", "type": "safe", "title": "Beneficio garantizado", "reward": "Menor tasa asegurada."}]}, "correct_answer": {"correctOptionId": "a"}}

opportunity_cost.content_shape: content.scenario — string (displayed as soft indigo card); content.options (or resolveOptions fallback: choices, scenarios, plans, offers, items, cases, models, portfolios) — array of {id: string, text?: string, title?: string, label?: string, name?: string, benefits?: string[], description?: string, icon?: string}. Renderer detects rich data via content.options.some(opt => opt.benefits || opt.title || opt.description) — if true, shows Analysis panel with compare-gains-vs-lose table; if false, simple option select
opportunity_cost.answer_shape: correct_answer.correctOptionId (string) — the canonical chosen option id. Aliases: correctChoiceId, selectedId, selectedOptionId, bestOptionId, preferredOption, chosenOption, betterOption, correctChoice, chosenOptionId (full extractCorrectId list of ~80). Grader uses optionIdMatches() with prefix stripping for tolerance
render_gotchas: options [] empty or not provided — renderer gracefully falls back to fallback message but submission handler still runs. If no options resolved, component should skip gracefully but user can still submit with null → validateAnswer returns true (falsy intent)

benefits array missing — hasRichData check fails even if title/description present. Must provide benefits[] (even empty) to trigger analysis panel. If absent, analysis section doesn't render (confusing UX)
scenario undefined — optional but if missing and no decision context, user sees blank blue card at top

options with plain text field instead of structured data — if options.find(opt => !opt.benefits && !opt.title) returns true, hasRichData = false, no Analysis shown even if some options have rich data. All-or-nothing flag → mixing plain + rich breaks UX
correctOptionIds plural array — if present, grader rejects single-selection submissions. opportunity_cost is single-select via selectedOption state; use singular correctOptionId only
opportunity_cost.canonical_example: {"content": {"scenario": "Elegir opción A: más dinero rápido vs Opción B: crecimiento a largo plazo", "options": [{"id": "a", "text": "Opción A", "title": "Ganancia Rápida", "description": "Efectivo en 3 meses", "icon": "💰", "benefits": ["Liquidez inmediata", "Sin riesgo"]}, {"id": "b", "text": "Opción B", "title": "Inversión Largo Plazo", "description": "Retorno 2 años", "icon": "📈", "benefits": ["Mayor retorno esperado", "Interés compuesto"]}]}, "correct_answer": {"correctOptionId": "b"}}

market_reaction.content_shape: content.headline — string (newspaper-style breaking news box); content.question — string (prediction prompt in indigo callout); content.options — array of {id: string, text?: string, label?: string, icon?: string} (2x2 grid by default). Renderer reads content.explanation — string (optional, shown only after feedback if present). Options are hard-coded prediction outcomes: id values like 'up', 'down', 'stable' are typical but any string works
market_reaction.answer_shape: correct_answer.correctOptionId (string) — the prediction outcome id (e.g., 'up', 'a', 'increase'). Aliases: correctChoiceId, correctId, choiceId, selectedId, predictedId, correctPrediction. Grader line 82 explicitly checks option.id === exercise.correct_answer?.correctOptionId for is-correct visual state; uses optionIdMatches() fallback if direct match fails
render_gotchas: headline or question empty — renders blank boxes, breaks UX. Market context is critical.
options missing text/label — option renders as '📊' with no label text. Must provide text or label key.
options.length != 4 — renderer always uses 2x2 grid CSS (grid-cols-2). If 3 options: 1 orphan in second row. If 5+: overflow outside viewport. Must be exactly 4 or adjust grid dynamically

correct_answer.correctOptionId not found in options — grader still runs optionIdMatches() so submission can pass, but UI never highlights as-correct on feedback. User sees no is-correct visual, only is-wrong or is-dimmed → silent grading failure
explanation missing — after feedback, no explanation box renders. Component expects content.explanation to exist; if null, feedback omits educational context (confusing for learning)

Option ids not matching grader expectations — if option.id is 'option_up' but correct_answer.correctOptionId is 'up', optionIdMatches() falls back to prefix-strip and compares 'up' === 'up' (via normalizeId). This works but is fragile
market_reaction.canonical_example: {"content": {"headline": "Competidor anuncia reducción de precios en 15%", "question": "¿Cómo reaccionará el mercado?", "options": [{"id": "up", "text": "Precio Sube", "icon": "📈"}, {"id": "down", "text": "Precio Baja", "icon": "📉"}, {"id": "stable", "text": "Se Mantiene", "icon": "➡️"}, {"id": "volatile", "text": "Volatilidad", "icon": "⚡"}], "explanation": "La competencia agresiva típicamente presiona precios a la baja y aumenta volatilidad."}, "correct_answer": {"correctOptionId": "down"}}

decision_challenge.content_shape: content.options (or resolveOptions fallback: choices, scenarios, plans, offers, items, cases, models, portfolios) — array of {id: string, text?: string, label?: string, name?: string, title?: string}. Renderer shuffles options on mount (Fisher-Yates). Displays grid 1-col (odd count) or 2-col (even) via isOddCount = shuffled.length % 2 !== 0. component.correctId extracted via extractCorrectId(exercise.correct_answer) used to highlight on feedback only (not during selection)
decision_challenge.answer_shape: correct_answer.correctOptionId (string) — the canonical best choice id. Aliases: correctChoiceId, correctId, choiceId, selectedId, selectedOptionId, bestOptionId, preferredOption, recommendedOptionId, betterChoiceId, betterStrategyId, optimalOptionId, decidedOptionId, chosenOptionId, chosenStrategy, selectedApproach, correctApproach, etc. (full ~80-alias extractCorrectId list). Grader uses String(id) === String(correctId) after extractCorrectId resolves alias, returns false if no match
render_gotchas: options [] empty — GenericChoice gracefully falls back to skip card 'Continuar'. User can bypass without answering. No validation error on submitAnswer() — returns true (always correct when no options)
options present but no option.text field — OptionCard child renders option.text as display. If undefined, renders blank button text. Grader still works (id comparison) but UI is broken

correctOptionId not found in options — grader comparison String(answer) === String(correctId) fails to match. User gets is-wrong even if logically correct. No fuzzy prefix-match in decision_challenge case (unlike risk_reward/opportunity_cost); uses strict String equality. Fragile if option.id format varies

resolveOptions fallback keys missing — if content.options is not provided, GenericChoice tries ['options', 'choices', 'scenarios', 'plans', 'offers', 'items', 'cases', 'models', 'portfolios']. If none exist, shuffled.length === 0 → graceful fallback, not error

Multi-select shape (correctOptionIds array) — grader checks for this in line 470–475 of validateAnswer. decision_challenge sent to 'option-based' case. If correctOptionIds array is provided instead of correctOptionId, grader treats as multi-select (user must pick ALL ids in the set), not single-select. This breaks single-answer UX expectation
decision_challenge.canonical_example: {"content": {"scenario": "Tu amigo tiene una oportunidad de negocio. ¿Cuál es la mejor acción?", "options": [{"id": "a", "text": "Invertir capital y tiempo en investigación antes de decidir"}, {"id": "b", "text": "Saltar inmediatamente sin validar mercado"}, {"id": "c", "text": "Ignorar completamente la oportunidad"}]}, "correct_answer": {"correctOptionId": "a"}}

budget_builder.content_shape: content.categories: [{id, name, label, text, title, allocated?, target?, max?, maxValue?}] (array) OR content.items: [{id, icon?, text, label, name, title, cost}] (array for legacy drag-drop). Also: content.scenario (string), content.instruction (string), content.budget (number), content.total_budget (number), content.total_income (number), content.totalIncome, content.income, content.monthlyIncome, content.amount (all numeric, fallback chain). For slider mode: categories[] required with id field. content.min_dca (number, optional, triggers DCA validation). Legacy mode: items[] required with id,cost.
budget_builder.answer_shape: correct_answer.allocation: Record<categoryId, number> OR correct_answer.allocations: Record<categoryId, number> (nested object with category IDs as keys, amounts as values; component sends Record<string, number>). Also accepts extractCorrectId aliases (correctOptionId, etc.) for option-based validation. Fallback: normalizeBudgetCorrect() checks .allocation/.allocations/.minCategory+.minAmount/.isValid/.isValidAllocation/.isValidBudget. If direct numeric keys exist (e.g., {c1: 100, c2: 250}), treated as allocation map. Answer MUST sum to totalIncome for newSchema sliders. answer_shape primary: "correct_answer.allocation: Record<categoryId, number>" or singular key e.g. "correct_answer.allocation" (accepted aliases: allocations)
render_gotchas: content.categories[] present but empty → renders fallback no-data screen (line 172-186), does NOT crash
content.items[] present AND content.categories[] present → legacy drag-drop takes priority (line 61); new schema sliders never render if items exist
content.categories[].allocated missing → initializes to 0 in newSchema (line 71), visible as slider starts at 0
Slider validation: totalAllocated > totalIncome triggers 'over budget' error (line 132), Submit returns early, grader never invoked

DCA validation: if content.min_dca is set, component searches for category.name matching 'dca' OR 'inversion' (case-insensitive, line 121-122); if not found, DCA check skipped silently. Grader never sees minCategory+minAmount shape.

correct_answer.validation: 'any_allocation' (string key in real lessons, e.g., line 365 adventure_5/saga_3/topic_19/lesson_6.json) → normalizeBudgetCorrect() returns null, component-side validation only, grader returns true (line 863)
Drag-drop legacy: items[] without cost field → renders '0' cost (line 440 fallback). answer: Record<itemId, categoryName> (string, not number).
Tolerance: correct_answer.tolerance missing → defaults to 0.01 in grader (line 877), tight tolerance for allocation matching

concept_builder.content_shape: content.concepts OR content.items OR content.components OR content.pieces OR content.blocks OR content.steps OR content.buildingBlocks OR content.building_blocks OR content.elements OR content.options OR content.parts OR content.tags (array of {id, label, text, name, title, item, word, term, value, type?}). content.instruction (string) or content.question (string). If multi-select mode (see answer_shape), component reads correct_answer.correctOptionIds/.selectedIds/.componentIds/.correctComponentIds/.essentialIds/.correctConceptIds/.requiredIds/.correctIds/.correctComponents/.correctStatementIds to detect subset mode (line 36-38).
concept_builder.answer_shape: Sequencing (ordering): answer is string[] of ordered block IDs (line 92). CANONIC: correct_answer.sequence OR correct_answer.correctSequence OR correct_answer.order OR correct_answer.correctOrder (array of IDs). Multi-select (subset): answer is string[] of selected block IDs (line 69). CANONIC: correct_answer.correctOptionIds OR correct_answer.selectedIds OR correctComponentIds OR correctConceptIds OR requiredIds OR correctIds OR correctComponents OR correctStatementIds (array of IDs). Component picks mode by checking which key exists in correct_answer (line 38, SUBSET_KEYS list).
render_gotchas: rawSource: multi-fallback chain concepts|items|components|pieces|blocks|steps|buildingBlocks|building_blocks|elements|options|parts|tags (line 31-33). If NONE present → blocks=[], renders empty screen (line 115-154 for subset mode, or blank block row for ordering)
isSelectMode detection: ANY key from SUBSET_KEYS in correct_answer triggers multi-select mode (line 38). Sequencing and subset modes MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE. If both keys somehow present, subset wins.
Shuffle: every render/retry reshuffles blocks (line 46-50). User cannot rely on order matching visual position.
Sequencing: component reads blocks.map(b => b.id) in current order, sends that as answer (line 92), not original order from content.items
block.type === 'connector' renders as lp-chip text, not button (line 170-172, grayed text). Non-connector blocks render as lp-token and highlight green on success.
Empty rawSource → no blocks rendered, but no error screen shown (unlike BudgetBuilder). Component just shows empty flow for ordering mode.
pickText() fallback chain: label→text→name→title→item→word→term→value (line 136). Missing all keys → renders empty string.
Tolerance missing from grader: sequencing does exact ID match (line 594), no numeric tolerance applied

portfolio_builder.content_shape: Legacy (assets) mode: content.assets: [{id, name, label, text, title, color?, risk? (0-10 scale)}] (array). Options (selection) mode: content.options: [{id, text, label, name, title}] (array). Also: content.scenario (string), content.instruction (string), content.criteria: [string] (array of criterion strings). isLegacy = Array.isArray(rawAssets) && rawAssets.length > 0 (line 47). isOptions = !isLegacy && Array.isArray(rawOptions) && rawOptions.length > 0 (line 48).
portfolio_builder.answer_shape: Legacy (allocation): answer is Record<assetId, number> (0-100 percentage per asset). CANONIC KEY in correct_answer: extractCorrectId() first (option ID). If found, compares picked asset ID. Allocation mode: answer sums to 100 (line 970-971). Options (selection) mode: answer is {selectedOptionId: 100} (line 128, submit formats as object). CANONIC: correct_answer.correctOptionId or any extractCorrectId() alias. Allocation expects: answer keys match content.assets[].id, values sum to ~100% (tolerance 0.01).
render_gotchas: No-data fallback: if !isLegacy && !isOptions, renders alertcircle + continue button (line 153-168), no render attempt on empty/missing assets/options
pickText() for assets: label→text→name→title (line 53, fallback to String(a.id))
Asset color default: a.color || '#5b6ef5' (indigo fallback, line 54)
Risk default: a.risk ?? 5 (numeric, line 55)
Options mode colors: cycled from COLOR_PALETTE by idx%4 (line 61, hardcoded 6-color array replaces asset.color)
Legacy validation: allocatedTotal !== totalAmount → submit disabled (line 151, line 123 validates exact match, tolerance 0.01 in grader)
Options validation: !selectedOptionId → submit disabled (line 151), must pick exactly one
PIE CHART SVG (legacy only): computed on-the-fly from allocation state, no content shape for pie data. Renders null if allocation[asset.id] === 0 (line 217, no slice rendered).
correct_answer.validation field (e.g., 'any_allocation', line 365 real lesson) NOT checked by grader or component, purely for lesson metadata
Options mode: can only submit {selectedOptionId: 100} format, not a split allocation

bill_splitter.content_shape: content.people: [{id, name, label, text, title}] (array of people who share). content.items: [{id, price (number), text, label, name, title}] (array of items/costs). Renderer computes: total = items.reduce((sum, item) => sum + item.price, 0) (line 27). tip (slider 0-30%, default 15%, line 22). mode: 'equitable' (split total equally) or 'proportional' (split by item assignment, line 20).
bill_splitter.answer_shape: EXPLORER/SIMULATOR TYPE: answer is Record<personId, number> (amount each person owes after split calculation and tip). correct_answer shape: grader accepts extractCorrectId() OR extractCorrectNumeric() if set, but most lessons omit correct_answer. Exploratory default (line 1082): if correctId or correctVal both undefined, return true (always pass). If correct_answer.tolerance set (numeric comparison), uses it; else defaults 0.01.
render_gotchas: ALWAYS GRADABLE=FALSE for this type: line 1071-1082 in grader validates presence of correctId/correctVal ONLY; if neither exist, return true. Bill splitter is predominantly exploratory simulator.

Mode toggle: equitable → automatic per-person calc grandTotal/people.length (line 61-64). Proportional → assignment-driven (line 67-76), requires all items assigned before submit (line 85-93 component validation).
People and items pulled directly from content (line 25-26), no fallback chain. Missing = empty array.
TipAmount: (total * tip) / 100 (line 28). Slider bounds 0-30%, step 5 (line 203).
Equitable mode: Submit always enabled, calculates and validates only that tip is 0-30 (line 84, no item assignment check for equitable, line 85-93 only checks proportional)
Proportional mode: each item must appear in exactly one person's assignments (line 86-93). If not all items assigned, Submit returns early without invoking grader.
calculateSplits() is deterministic: same inputs → same splits. No randomization.
Grader feedback on bill_splitter is NEVER shown; only component-side success/error states (line 253-268 feedback card, line 257-258 uses mode-specific i18n keys)
answers sent to grader: splits object {personId: amount} from calculateSplits(), NOT the assignments or mode. Grader never sees which mode was used.

interest_calculator.content_shape: content.defaultPrincipal (number), content.defaultRate (number), content.defaultTime (number), content.parameters.principal (number), content.parameters.annualRate (number), content.maxPrincipal (number), content.maxRate (number), content.maxTime (number), content.type ('simple'|'compound')
interest_calculator.answer_shape: correct_answer.value (number) OR exploratory if answer is object {principal, rate, time}; canonical: correct_answer.value (single numeric value or omitted for simulator mode)
render_gotchas: answer.object form {principal, rate, time} ALWAYS grades true (line 1021 useLessonState.ts: 'if (answer && typeof answer === 'object') return true') — simulator mode, not gradable
correct_answer.value missing or null → always returns true (line 1021-1029 fallback)
confusing content.parameters.annualRate with content.defaultRate — renderer uses defaultRate first, fallback to content.parameters.annualRate (line 29-30)
content.type 'simple' vs 'compound' MUST match for chart rendering (lines 74-76, 248, 267)

estimation_slider.content_shape: content.problem (string), content.question (string), content.min (number), content.max (number), content.step (number), content.unit (string), content.ranges (array of {id, minValue|min, maxValue|max}), content.correctValue (number), content.tolerance (number), content.range.min (number), content.range.max (number), content.range.step (number)
estimation_slider.answer_shape: correct_answer.value (number) OR correct_answer.correctValue (number); canonical key: correct_answer.value (number within tolerance). Alias: correct_answer.numericAnswer, correct_answer.correctValue, correct_answer.answer. Also accepts correct_answer with range keys: correct_answer.range {min, max}, correct_answer.min/max pair, correct_answer.rangeStart/rangeEnd
render_gotchas: content.ranges array present AND content.min/max missing → slider min/max extracted from ranges.minValue/maxValue bounds (line 22-24), NOT content.min/max directly
correct_answer.correctRangeId logic (line 692-700 useLessonState.ts) ONLY works if content.ranges array AND targetRange.minValue/maxValue defined; else fallback to numeric value
tolerance field reads from correct_answer.tolerance FIRST, then content.tolerance (line 49 EstimationSlider.tsx, line 730 useLessonState.ts)
component shows 'close' feedback at 2x tolerance (line 62 EstimationSlider.tsx) but grader only knows 'success' or 'error' (line 730-731)
unit field rendered inline but NOT transmitted to grader (purely display)

inflation_simulator.content_shape: content.product {basePrice (number), baseYear (number), name|label|text|title (string), icon (emoji string)}, content.inflationRate (number, as %), content.defaultYearStart (number), content.defaultYearEnd (number), content.minYear (number), content.maxYear (number)
inflation_simulator.answer_shape: correct_answer.yearStart (number) AND correct_answer.yearEnd (number) OR exploratory if none present. Canonical: object {yearStart, yearEnd} or exploratory (return true). useLessonState line 1074 treats 'inflation_simulator' as exploratory—if extractCorrectId/Numeric finds nothing, 'return true'
render_gotchas: component sends {yearStart, yearEnd} as answer; validator expects object OR checks for correctId/numeric value (line 1075-1082 useLessonState.ts)
no explicit correct_answer validation logic: falls through to line 1082 'return true' (simulators are exploratory by design)
content.product.name/label/text/title field — pickText() helper (line 6, 69) extracts whichever key is defined; renderer READS first match, not guaranteed order
baseYear MUST be within minYear/maxYear range or price calculation may show negative/inverted values (line 34-36)
correctAnswer shape (if provided): must use yearStart/yearEnd keys exactly, not 'startYear'/'endYear'

emergency_fund.content_shape: content.events (array of {id (string), description (string), options (array of {id (string), text|label|description (string), cost (number)})}), content.initialFund (number, starting balance)
emergency_fund.answer_shape: correct_answer.minBalance (number) OR correct_answer.minFund (number). Canonical: correct_answer.minBalance (minimum fund balance user must end with, >=0). Answer is Record<string, string> = {eventId: selectedOptionId, ...} OR array of decision IDs. Grader computes final balance by iterating events and subtracting costs of chosen options
render_gotchas: answer shape is Record<eventId, decisionId> (line 22 EmergencyFund.tsx, line 57 setDecisions) but grader expects object form AND uses event.id to look up (line 934-940 useLessonState.ts: 'const decisionId = userMap ? userMap[event.id] : ...')

component KEYS decisions by event.id (line 57: '[event.id]: decisionId') but if events array is indexed 0-N, Object.values() ordering FAILS—grader correctly handles this via event.id lookup (line 940), not index
correct_answer.minBalance numeric threshold: if user balance >= minBalance after all decisions, 'success', else 'error' (line 944-945)
content.events array MUST have options[].cost defined and numeric, else balance calculation skips (line 942 'Number(option.cost || 0)')
missing or empty events array → component renders 'Cargando emergencias...' (line 39-48), grader returns true (line 930)

tax_puzzle.content_shape: content.pieces: [{id, name/label, icon, min, max, step, description, defaultValue}], OR fallback content.options: [{id, text/label}], content.puzzle/instruction (title), content.puzzle/income/deductions/taxRate (used in calc display)
tax_puzzle.answer_shape: correct_answer.correctOptionId (string id, fallback case lines 456-479) for multiple-choice mode; Record<string, number> {pieceId: value} for slider mode (lines 27-30, 56). Primary key: correctOptionId (line 77 useLessonState.ts). Normalized via extractCorrectId() aliases: correctChoiceId, correctId, choiceId, betterOption, etc.
render_gotchas: pieces[] mode (sliders) submits Record<string,number> (line 56: onSubmit(pieces)) but grader validateAnswer() case 'tax_puzzle' uses extractCorrectId(), expecting string id, NOT numeric allocation. Fallback to multiple-choice (lines 75-138) if no pieces, but pieces present + no correctOptionId = grader returns true (line 479). Mismatch: renderer can send {income:100, deductions:50} but grader can't grade Record<string,number> against scalar correctOptionId.

options[] vs pieces[] detection: if content.pieces.length > 0, render slider mode; else if content.options.length > 0, render choice mode (lines 38, 75). Mixed data (both present) renders pieces first, ignoring options. No explicit type flag, ambiguous.
Calculation display reads pieces object keys directly (lines 39-45: pieces.income, pieces.deductions, pieces.taxRate) - if piece.id doesn't match these exact names, display breaks silently.

Multiple-choice fallback (lines 75-138) submits selectedOption (string id), which matches grader expectation, but uses separate fb state instead of shared feedback state, causing double-state bug if mixed with pieces mode.

salary_comparison.content_shape: content.offers: [{id, salary, benefits, location, growth}] (legacy, lines 39-40) OR content.options/optionA/optionB/offer_a/offer_b resolved via resolveOptions() (lines 44-48), normalized to [{id, company, description}]. content.scenario, content.question, content.instruction (optional, lines 116-131). Legacy: calculateScore() weights salary 40%, benefits 30%, location 15%, growth 15% (lines 56-64).
salary_comparison.answer_shape: correct_answer.correctOptionId (string offer id) or correct_answer.bestOffer (lines 951-953 useLessonState.ts). Primary key: extracted via extractCorrectId() with aliases bestChoiceId, recommendedOptionId, preferredOption, selectedId, etc. Matching is case-insensitive via optionIdMatches() (lines 154-167).
render_gotchas: isLegacy detection (line 33): Array.isArray(content.offers) && content.offers.length > 0. If offers=[] but options[] present, isLegacy=false and legacy features (score calc) not rendered. Real lessons use options[], not offers[].

resolveOptions() (line 44) may return empty array if content has no recognized structure (optionA, options, offer_a, etc.), triggering fallback (lines 89-107) which allows onNext() without selection. Graceful but masks missing data.
company field extraction (line 46): tries company ?? name ?? title ?? text in order. If all missing, renders empty header. No validation that extracted values are strings.
factors[] (line 37) used for legacy scoring but ignored in modern render (lines 200-206). Mismatch: legacy scorecard uses hardcoded factor labels, not from content.factors.
Multiple offers (3+) use 3-column grid (line 139), but CSS classes (lp-option--indigo, lp-option--amber, etc.) cycle via index, not content id. UI color order breaks if offers reordered.

debt_strategy.content_shape: Legacy mode (lines 34-36): content.debts [{id, balance, rate, minPayment}], content.monthlyPayment (scalar). Modern mode (lines 36-37): content.options via resolveOptions() (same as SalaryComparison), content.scenario, content.instruction. Legacy also reads content.scenario + content.instruction (lines 31-32) for fallback text.
debt_strategy.answer_shape: Legacy mode (isLegacy=true): correct_answer field is NOT read by component, submit() sends selectedStrategy string ('snowball'|'avalanche') to grader, which extracts strategy via extractCorrectId() and tries optionIdMatches(). Modern mode: correct_answer.correctOptionId (string option id). Grader case 'debt_strategy' (lines 461-480) treats answer as string, applies extractCorrectId() for multi-choice, falls back to true if no correctId defined (line 479).
render_gotchas: Legacy vs modern detection (line 34): isLegacy = Array.isArray(debts) && debts.length > 0. If debts=[] but options[] present, isMultipleChoice=true, legacy simulator NOT rendered. Two completely different UX paths.

Legacy simulator calculates both snowball + avalanche (lines 95-96) regardless of selectedStrategy, but only one compares to correctAnswer. If grader has no correctId defined for 'snowball'/'avalanche' string, always returns true (line 479 useLessonState), making both strategies equally correct.
Modern multiple-choice mode (lines 160-241): submit uses selectedOptionId string, but selectedStrategy state unused in this branch. Confusing state management.
Fallback (lines 136-155): if !isLegacy && !isMultipleChoice, renders error message + continue button, calling onNext() immediately. No correct_answer graded. Silently skips exercise.
simulateStrategy() memoized on [debts, monthlyPayment, isLegacy] (line 93), but debts object identity changes each render, causing recalc even if values unchanged.

Corpus example (lesson_5.json, line 246-272) uses debt_strategy with multiple options (not legacy debts array), but correct_answer has NO correctOptionId or strategy identifier—grader returns true silently.

savings_race.content_shape: content.goal (numeric, displayed in trophy header, line 38), content.strategies: [{id, name/label, description/detail, icon, speed (numeric multiplier)}] (lines 39-40, 129-166). No standard title/scenario field used, only goal.
savings_race.answer_shape: correct_answer field in grader (lines 1074-1082 useLessonState.ts): case 'savings_race' extracts correctId via extractCorrectId() (string strategy id) OR correctVal via extractCorrectNumeric() (numeric goal check). Answer submitted is selectedStrategy string (line 70: onSubmit(selectedStrategy)). Grader optionIdMatches() or numericMatch() applied. If no correct_answer defined, returns true (line 1082).
render_gotchas: Animation-driven UX: progress state (0-100%) driven by interval (line 63-75), NOT by component re-render. If exercise replaced mid-animation, cleanup (lines 32-36) clears interval, but if onSubmit() called async, interval continues updating state after unmount.
strategies[] index used for hue color assignment (line 131: hue = ['indigo','amber','emerald','coral'][index%4]), not strategy.id. Reordering strategies changes colors unexpectedly.
selectedStrategy state initially null (line 20), but handleStartRace() requires it non-null (line 48). If user clicks 'Start' without selecting, returns early silently. No error feedback.
speed multiplier (line 57): duration = 3000 / speed. If speed=0 or undefined, duration=Infinity, animation never completes. No validation.
Grader expects selectedStrategy string (strategy.id), but renderer never validates that submitted id exists in content.strategies array. If id malformed or missing, grader receives garbage string.

No lecciones de corpus encontradas aún usando savings_race (searches returned no .json files with type='savings_race'). Contract inferred from component code + grader case logic, untested against real data.

Progress bar uses transition-all duration-100 (line 114), but interval updates every stepDuration (line 75, ~30ms for 3s animation). Smooth visual but discontinuous state updates risk browser reflow thrashing.

Pairwise form (optionA/optionB) synthesizes letter ids 'A'/'B' but grader sees extractCorrectId() aliases → both string match works (line 154-167 optionIdMatches tolerance)
Using wrong key name: correctChoiceId vs correctOptionId → extractCorrectId has 80+ aliases (lines 49-144) so small variations OK, but test the actual key used in lesson JSON
targetIds as single id instead of array → spot_trap uses targetIds array but comparison uses targetIds array too; if sent as string will fail Set match (line 1046)

case_study.answer_shape: correct_answer.correctOptionId (primary) OR any of 80+ extractCorrectId() aliases (lines 49-144) — compareAnswer uses optionIdMatches() (lines 154-167)

story_mode.content_shape: content: {scenario?, question?, instruction?, choices?: [{id, text, next_page?}], options?: [{id, text}]} OR content.pages: [{id, text, character_mood?, choices?: [...]}] (legacy format, lines 43-80)
story_mode.answer_shape: correct_answer.correctOptionId OR extractCorrectId() aliases (lines 49-144) — conditional grading: if gradedCorrectId !== undefined, component calls onSubmit(choiceId) AND records decision (lines 127-131); if undefined, pure consumption tree (line 495)
render_gotchas: pages[] vs choices[] naming: component builds virtual pages from scenario+question+choices if pages[] absent (lines 43-80); mixing legacy 'pages' key with new fields causes duplication or overwrite
next_page: undefined → navigation ENDS, advances to next exercise; next_page: string → finds page by id; if not found, falls back to handleNext() (lines 114-119)
Graded decision (onSubmit with correctId) does NOT penalize — it just records decided={id, correct} and shows feedback (lines 127-130), then user can continue (line 234-237)
character_mood normalization: rawMood mapped via normalizeGesture(characterCode, mood) — invalid mood falls back (line 178)
If pages[] empty, auto-advances after 100ms debounce (lines 100-105) to prevent loops

roleplay_chat.content_shape: content: {scenario, instruction?, options: [{id, text}] OR choices: [...] OR responseOptions: [...] OR chatOptions: [...]} (line 63 fallback key search)
roleplay_chat.answer_shape: correct_answer.correctOptionId (primary) OR any extractCorrectId() alias (lines 49-144) — grader calls onSubmit(choiceId: string) and returns boolean isCorrect (line 92)
render_gotchas: options key variants: content.options > content.choices > content.responseOptions > content.chatOptions (line 63); if NONE present, renders 'No options available' with skip button (lines 187-196)
Answer is ALWAYS a single choiceId string (line 78), not array; multi-select not supported
feedback.success/feedback.error are optional; if missing, falls back to i18n defaults (lines 99-100)

Feedback state persists until handleContinue() called (line 115-126); if 'success' user calls onNext(), if 'error' removes last 2 messages and calls onRetry()
selectedChoiceId lock (line 76 'if (selectedChoiceId) return') prevents double-submission during delay
